name: CORTE
description: Research artifacts for CORTE: Compiling natural-language rules into reusable context monitors for mobile sensing, by Hang Su, Karol Nowakowski, and Masahiro Toyoura, University of Yamanashi. The primary derived benchmark contains 377,346 ExtraSensory records from 60 participants, 39 primitive concepts, 26 candidate composite situations (25 retained), and 104 researcher-authored queries (100 retained). The MyDigitalFootprint transfer benchmark contains 67,575 samples, 15 candidate situations (12 retained), and 48 retained queries. The release includes derived ternary labels, five participant-grouped folds, programs, queries, code, model configurations, saved JSON results, manuscript tables. Unzip the research archive into a new directory. See README.txt, the dataset card, and the reproduction guide. SHA-256 checksums are supplied. All 26 primary label columns were independently reconstructed for all 60 users; validation and saved-result checks are included. The primary saved result is 0.265 AUPRC and 0.883 trigger F1. These are retrospective, annotation-derived benchmarks. Per-record model prediction matrices are not included in this release. Original sensor datasets, private device logs, and model weights are excluded. Historical environment locks, immutable model revision hashes, and some training checkpoints were not retained; the guide describes the resulting reproducibility limits. No new GPU training or timing experiment is claimed.
